baseline.variant_facts:
The merchandise under consideration is a wooden furniture.. The product of CBP ruling N357951, as its facts describe it. The wooden furniture. is assembled in Canada using components sourced from United States, Germany, China and Canada.

The black walnut hardwood, textile backing and glue are produced in United States. The metal threaded inserts and screws are sourced from Germany. The magnets are sourced from China. The white oak hardwood are produced in Canada. 

Final assembly in Canada: assemble the parts into the finished good.

Tariff classifications given with the product (HTSUS; the product's own codes, not verified by CBP): the wooden furniture. (the finished good), 9403.60.8093; the black walnut hardwood (made in United States), 4407.99; the textile backing (made in United States), 5907.00; the glue (made in United States), 3506.91; the metal threaded inserts (made in Germany), 7318.16; the screws (made in Germany), 7318.12; the magnets (made in China), 8505.11; the white oak hardwood (made in Canada), 4407.91.

prediction.decisive_step: Final assembly and production of the wooden furniture in Canada
prediction.reasoning: The finished wooden furniture is classified in subheading 9403.60. Under 19 CFR 102.20(r), the rule for 9403.10-9403.89 requires a change from any other subheading. All foreign materials (4407.99, 5907.00, 3506.91, 7318.16, 7318.12, 8505.11) meet this tariff shift in Canada.
